checks.detail: import skimage.data -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'skimage'. Upstream's target is unavailable, so a deterministic chromatix-bundled siemens_star is substituted and upstream's published trajectory -- a property of the cat photograph -- is recorded for reference rather than asserted.
checks.name: scikit_image_is_not_available_in_the_pinned_environment

checks.detail: the siemens_star target is (300, 300), matching the model's (300, 300) grid -- the same shape upstream's cat crop has
checks.name: the_substituted_target_matches_the_model_grid

checks.detail: binarize() of a uniform(0, 1) draw takes 2 distinct values [0.0, 1.0], with 50.21% on. The DMD really is modelled as a binary device in the forward pass.
checks.name: binarize_produces_exactly_two_levels_zero_and_one

checks.detail: the gradient through binarize is (300, 300) with magnitudes in [5.078e-12, 2.130e-06] and only 0.000% of pixels exactly zero. A true sign/round would give an identically zero gradient and the optimization could not move at all -- so chromatix.ops.binarize carries a surrogate gradient, which is the whole point of this example and is only establishable by measurement.
checks.name: binarize_has_a_non_zero_surrogate_gradient_at_every_pixel

checks.detail: initial correlation 0.478801 and loss 0.941535, against upstream's 0.73058045 and 0.91078347 for the cat target. Both are in [0, 1] as their definitions require. Note the two do NOT sum to 1 (1.42 here, 1.64 upstream): optax.cosine_distance and this example's hand-written normalised inner product are different quantities, so the 'correlation' reported alongside the loss is not 1 - loss. Absolute values are not asserted because they are properties of the target image.
checks.name: the_initial_loss_and_correlation_are_both_physical_and_recorded

checks.detail: correlation 0.478800 -> 0.739627 over 400 Adam steps at lr = 2.0, best 0.739627. Upstream reports 0.730580 -> 0.863588 on its own target.
checks.name: the_optimization_raises_the_correlation_substantially

checks.detail: by iteration 40 the correlation has already reached 0.735476 of its final 0.739627, i.e. most of the gain arrives in the first 10% of the run. Upstream's trajectory shows the same shape (0.7306 -> 0.8616 -> 0.8636), so the saturation is a property of the method rather than of the target.
checks.name: the_correlation_gain_saturates_early_as_upstream_shows

checks.detail: the running maximum of the correlation is monotone over all 400 steps
checks.name: the_running_maximum_correlation_never_falls

checks.detail: RMS change in the continuous amplitude parameter is 16.5044 and its range grew to [-39.8724, 41.8230] from the initial [0, 1). The optimizer moves the continuous variable; only its binarization reaches the field.
checks.name: the_continuous_amplitude_moved_far_from_its_uniform_initialisation

checks.detail: correlation with the target peaks at z = 130000 of the 20 swept planes, which is the design distance z = 130000. Correlation there is 0.739620 against 0.484345 at the worst plane. A 1D z produces the whole through-focus stack in one call, which is what the example's final figure shows.
checks.name: the_hologram_is_sharpest_at_the_design_distance

demonstrates: chromatix.ops.binarize as a differentiable hard threshold (surrogate gradient) inside amplitude_change, asm_propagate(mode='same') with a scalar or 1D z, and optax.cosine_distance as a hologram loss.
title: Computer Generated Holography using a Digital Micromirror Device
